subject: Materials Science
title: Elastic Modulus: Measuring Stiffness
description: A fast breakdown of Elastic Modulus: Measuring Stiffness for builders.

hook.text: A diamond barely deflects under load. Rubber stretches to ten times its length. Stiffness varies enormously.

buildup.text: Young's modulus (E) is the slope of the stress-strain curve in the elastic region — stiffness in one number.

discovery.text: Steel: 200 GPa. Aluminum: 70 GPa. Rubber: 0.01 GPa. The bonds between atoms determine stiffness.

twist.text: You can't change a metal's modulus by heat treatment or alloying — it's set by atomic bonding.

climax.text: Aircraft designers pick materials by specific modulus — stiffness divided by density — to save weight.

punchline.text: Stiffness is baked into the atoms — no processing trick can change it.

quiz.question: What determines a material's elastic modulus?
options: The strength of its atomic bonds
